description: Every memory reservation of the course board, with its owner and source, as the live device tree states it. ci/dt_memory.py checks it against the extraction named in 'evidence' (and any new extraction from a board), and checks manifest/dsp-cores.json against both: each DSP's carve-out and DMA pool, local memories, MSMC, and shared DDR.

reserved_memory.reason: Inter-RTOS IPC shared memory (vrings between RTOS cores). No device-tree node uses it, but the device-manager firmware on MCU R5F core 0 (TI's IPC echo test with Sciserver, PSDK 11.02.00.07) does at run time: TI's DSP echo firmware messaged it through here until its IPC heap ran out and TI-SCI device management stopped answering, which only a reboot cleared (release/evidence/task-013/20261019T095039Z). No course firmware may use it; every DSP's protection denies it (docs/safety.md).
reserved_memory.source: k3-j721e-beagleboneai64.dts in BeagleBoard.org kernel 6.18.55-arm64-k3-r59 (live device tree, release/evidence/task-012/20261019T094327Z/dt-memory.json); release/evidence/task-013/20261019T095039Z/mcu_r5f0_0-dm-trace.txt

srams.reason: MCU on-chip SRAM. Linux's mmio-sram driver binds it but no node allocates from it. No DSP contract region uses it.
srams.source: k3-j721e-beagleboneai64.dts in BeagleBoard.org kernel 6.18.55-arm64-k3-r59 (live device tree, release/evidence/task-012/20261019T094327Z/dt-memory.json)

srams.reason: MSMC SRAM. Linux's mmio-sram driver binds it but no node allocates from it; atf-sram@0 (128 KiB) holds ARM Trusted Firmware. The top 64 KiB (0x707F0000) is outside the node: TI's linker files give it to the DMSC firmware.

usable.source: this node minus atf-sram@0; TI PDK 11.02.01.08 linker_c66_freertos_common.inc (MSMC3)
usable.note: Not owned by any core. Every DSP's protection denies it (docs/safety.md) until a partition gives each core its own slice.
